transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-14
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Samir Rao (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Kyverna CISO), Rahul Patel (Kyverna Platform), Tom Nguyen (Kyverna Legal)

Summary: Quick security posture intake to decide between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment. Customer focused on SOC2/ISO alignment, BYOK KMS, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs and long-term data retention policies.

Topics: SOC2 / ISO readiness, SSO and SAML integration, RBAC model mapping, audit log ingestion/retention, KMS/BYOK requirements, data residency and retention windows, pilot criteria and timeline.

Transcript:
00:00 - Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll run about 45 to 60 minutes, just wanted to understand your security posture and constraints, maybe start with a quick intro from each team member
00:12 - Lena Ortiz: hi lena here, im the ciso at kyverna, we handle compliance across product and infra, we're evaluating options for hosting inference for a PHI-adjacent workload so security and retention are top of mind
00:24 - Rahul Patel: rahul, platform eng, i'll be owning the integration and network stuff, also looking at latency/cost tradeoffs since this will hit customer-facing apis
00:35 - Tom Nguyen: tom, legal, i'll be focused on data retention obligations and contractual encryption requirements, happy to listen
00:40 - Diego Ruiz: diego from redwood, i'll take the technical deep-dive later on, we can map features to requirements as we go
00:48 - Maya Chen: perfect, lena, can you give us the high level of compliance boxes you need checked? soc2, iso, anything else?
01:02 - Lena Ortiz: SOC2 type two is a must, we also have a roadmap to ISO 27001 but not required day one, we need to see evidence of controls, pen test, and preferably detailed audit logs. also we have EU data residency requirements for eu customers
01:20 - Maya Chen: yep understood. we have SOC2 type II, we can share report and pen test. we support hosted, dedicated reserved pools, and private vpc/on-prem packages — do you have a preference now?
01:35 - Lena Ortiz: preference is private if we can get BYOK, that addresses legal. if private is too heavy we'll consider dedicated with strict VPC isolation and kms integration. hosted is a last resort for non-sensitive workloads
01:50 - Rahul Patel: can you explain redwood's BYOK story? we currently use aws-kms and azure keyvault across products
02:05 - Samir Rao: sure — we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault for the private control plane and Dedicated in most regions. for hosted we offer envelope encryption and a managed KMS option; BYOK for hosted is more limited today, we can discuss specific cloud pairs
02:20 - Rahul Patel: limited for hosted — can you expand? like which operations are BYOK-protected (model artifacts vs cache vs logs)?
02:33 - Diego Ruiz: good q. model checkpoints and S3 artifacts can be encrypted with your CMKs, runtime KV cache is ephemeral but we can wrap the master key, audit logs and metrics are encrypted at rest and we can route logs to your SIEM via secure forwarding — though hosted default retention is short, so for long-term retention we'd recommend Dedicated or Private with your own log sinks
03:00 - Lena Ortiz: audit logging is huge for us. we need immutable, tamper-evident logs, and retention for seven years for certain regulated customers — do you have WORM or immutability features?
03:15 - Maya Chen: we support write-once retention policies via Customer log sinks (like AWS S3 with Object Lock) in Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted can forward logs but doesn't provide Object Lock by default
03:33 - Tom Nguyen: also need chain of custody and proof of deletion for data subject requests — if a user requests deletion, how does redwood ensure cached KV or logs are removed?
03:45 - Diego Ruiz: we have KV cache eviction and we can flush per-tenant caches on request in Dedicated/Private; for hosted we can perform scoped redaction but deletion timelines depend on retention windows and any backups — we can include deletion certification in contractual terms for Dedicated/Private pilots
04:05 - Rahul Patel: about RBAC — we use LDAP + SAML for SSO, and want role-based separation between platform engineers and app owners, are you able to map to our roles and integrate with SAML assertions?
04:20 - Samir Rao: yes, we integrate SSO via SAML 2.0 and support IDP-initiated and SP-initiated flows. RBAC mapping can be configured per-organization and you can inject groups/claims to map to Redwood roles. we also have audit trails for admin actions
04:40 - Lena Ortiz: great. what about session recording and admin access monitoring? we need to know when someone escalates to root or runs admin jobs
04:52 - Diego Ruiz: admin actions are logged with user, ip, and timestamp; we can stream those logs to SIEM. session recording for shell-level access on private is possible if you host the ops plane; for hosted console sessions we have event-level records but not full terminal session recording out of the box
05:10 - Maya Chen: on encryption in transit, we use mTLS for service-to-service within Redwood clusters and TLS 1.2+ for client comms — do you need dedicated cert management?
05:24 - Rahul Patel: we manage certs via vault, would rather use our PKI where possible
05:29 - Samir Rao: for Dedicated/Private we can integrate with your PKI for cert issuance and rotation. hosted uses our managed certs but can support mutual TLS for customer connections in many configurations
05:45 - Tom Nguyen: contractually we need data residency clauses and an agreed-retention schedule; right now our legal asks for 7-year retention on transaction logs and 30-day retention for raw utterances unless elevated via customer consent — can your platform separate those classes?
06:05 - Diego Ruiz: yes, data classification is supported. we can tier retention: short-term ephemeral store for raw utterances, long-term archival for transaction logs with S3 lifecycle rules, and per-tenant retention policies in Dedicated/Private
06:25 - Lena Ortiz: penalty for data leakage is high — also curious about breach notification SLA and whether you have SOC2 incident response playbooks we can align to
06:38 - Maya Chen: we can share our incident response playbook and our SOC2 will include incident response controls. breach notification timelines are negotiable in contract but we aim for 72-hour notification for confirmed incidents
06:50 - Rahul Patel: can you do a quick sketch of network topology for Dedicated vs Private? especially around VPC peering, egress controls, and whether we can use Transit Gateway
07:05 - Diego Ruiz: sure — Dedicated is hosted in our infra but we create customer-specific VPCs with strict security groups and optional NAT egress; Private gives you the customer-managed control plane where you can place instances inside your VPC and use Transit Gateway or direct connect, we can share diagrams after call
07:30 - Lena Ortiz: what about model provenance and tamper resistance for models — we need an audit trail for model versions served to production for compliance
07:42 - Samir Rao: we keep model version manifests, signed artifacts, and deployment records; those are included in audit logs with checksums. for Private we can also integrate signing via your PKI for an extra layer
07:58 - Tom Nguyen: any third-party pen tests? who performs them and how often?
08:08 - Maya Chen: we have annual third-party tests and can share the redacted reports. we also do internal appsec and infra scanning quarterly
08:18 - Rahul Patel: are there any limits on encrypting inference outputs? e.g., embeddings stored in vector DBs — we plan to hash and encrypt those but want to ensure keys never leave our control
08:30 - Diego Ruiz: for Private and Dedicated we support CMK-wrapped keys and you can keep master keys in KMS; embeddings and artifacts can be encrypted with your keys before they leave your environment for extra assurance
08:45 - Lena Ortiz: ok great. pilot criteria — what do you need from us to sign off on a small dedicated pilot?
08:55 - Maya Chen: typical asks: 1) provide SOC2 and pen test, 2) share the VPC diagram and allow us a short architecture review, 3) define success metrics (latency, cost per 1k tokens, availability), 4) schedule a Canaries run or load test with your sample traffic
09:18 - Rahul Patel: timeline — we're aiming to choose a vendor by end of month, pilot in august, prod by q4. is that realistic?
09:30 - Diego Ruiz: yes that timeline is reasonable for Dedicated; Private may take longer depending on procurement and network approvals, but we can kick off security paperwork in parallel
09:42 - Tom Nguyen: legal would like a draft addendum for data processing and KMS obligations before negotiation
09:50 - Maya Chen: we will route a starter DPA and a KMS addendum draft. we'll also include a summary of supported deployment modes and the scoping doc
10:02 - Maya Chen: are there any remaining questions?
10:07 - Lena Ortiz: one more — retention for backups: how long are backups retained and can we exclude certain buckets from backups?
10:18 - Samir Rao: backups follow the retention policy in Dedicated/Private and can be scoped per-tenant; we can exclude specific data classes and provide deletion certifications when asked
10:30 - Rahul Patel: can you provide SLA numbers for RTO/RPO for Dedicated?
10:38 - Diego Ruiz: yes, Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and we can provide target RTO/RPO in the pilot SOW, we'll attach specific numbers depending on the committed capacity
10:50 - Maya Chen: ok great, recap next steps: we'll send SOC2 and pen test, draft DPA & KMS addendum, schedule architecture deep-dive, and provide pricing for pilot.
11:05 - Tom Nguyen: that sounds good, thanks everyone
11:10 - Lena Ortiz: thanks, looking forward to receiving docs
11:15 - Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and docs

Meeting end.
